title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The gap between UK food exports and imports has hit its widest point since 2000, reaching a £21bn deficit. Industry leaders are now urging the government to prioritize domestic produce for national security as Brexit, global conflict, and tariffs strain trade. Meanwhile, in South America, Bolivia faces a tough economic crossroads. As its fossil gas boom fades, the country is grappling with rising inflation and trying to determine if relying on commodity exports like soy and gold is a sustainable path forward.

In the automotive world, BMW is sharing more details on its upcoming i3 sedan. Built on the new Neue Klasse platform, the car is expected to offer a range of up to 468 miles. Elsewhere in EV tech, the gap in charging speeds is widening. China has demonstrated a new LFP battery capable of charging from 10 to 70 percent in just 4.5 minutes, highlighting a significant lead over current US charging infrastructure.

In tech news, Meta's Muse filesystem was briefly exposed, giving some users a rare look at the inner workings of an AI chatbot. If you are noticing your iPhone acting sluggish, it might be time to check your battery health, as degradation is a common culprit for declining performance over time.

Finally, some fascinating science and engineering updates. Researchers have finally corrected a typo in a 19th-century record, solving a mystery about a geomagnetic storm that delayed a train in 1841. Looking to the future, a startup called Star Catcher is preparing to test space lasers designed to beam energy between two separate spacecraft for the first time.
